questions.question: The committee have decided to postpone the meeting until next Monday.
questions.solution: In standard exam usage, 'committee' is treated here as a single unit, so the singular verb 'has' is required: 'The committee has decided...'
questions.shortTrick: Singular collective noun acting as one unit → singular verb.

questions.question: Each of the applicants were asked to submit two recent photographs.
questions.solution: 'Each' is singular, so it takes 'was', not 'were'.
questions.shortTrick: Each/every/either/neither generally takes a singular verb.

questions.question: By the time the manager arrived, the staff already completed the inventory check.
questions.solution: The earlier of two past actions should normally be in past perfect: 'the staff had already completed'.

questions.question: She is responsible of preparing the weekly performance report.
questions.solution: The correct collocation is 'responsible for', not 'responsible of'.

questions.question: Rohan is an university graduate with two years of banking experience.
questions.solution: 'University' begins with the consonant sound /juː/, so 'a university' is correct.
questions.shortTrick: Choose article by sound, not spelling.

questions.question: The new policy aims to reduce paperwork, improving transparency and to speed up approvals.
questions.solution: The list should be parallel: 'to reduce..., improve..., and speed up...' or 'reducing..., improving..., and speeding...'.
questions.shortTrick: Items joined in a list should have the same grammatical form.

questions.question: Neither of the two officers submitted their report before the deadline.
questions.solution: In traditional competitive-exam grammar, singular 'neither' takes a singular pronoun: 'his or her report'.
questions.shortTrick: Neither/either → singular agreement in exam grammar.

questions.question: The number of digital transactions this year is higher than last year.
questions.solution: A number must be compared with a number: 'higher than that of last year'.

questions.question: If he would have checked the figures carefully, he would not have made the error.
questions.solution: In a third conditional, the if-clause takes past perfect: 'If he had checked...'.
questions.shortTrick: If + had + V3, would have + V3.

questions.question: The customer spoke polite to the executive despite the long delay.
questions.solution: The verb 'spoke' must be modified by the adverb 'politely'.

questions.question: The branch received fewer information about the revised procedure than expected.
questions.solution: 'Information' is uncountable; use 'less information', not 'fewer information'.

questions.question: Although the road was flooded, but the delivery team reached the village on time.
questions.solution: Do not use 'although' and 'but' together in this construction. Remove 'but'.

questions.question: The company avoided to disclose the details until the investigation was complete.
questions.solution: 'Avoid' is followed by a gerund: 'avoided disclosing'.

questions.question: The report, which findings were discussed yesterday, will be published next week.
questions.solution: Possession requires 'whose': 'the report, whose findings were discussed...'.

questions.question: The bank launched a campaign to ______ customers about common forms of online fraud.
questions.solution: 'Educate' means to give knowledge or instruction and fits the purpose of an awareness campaign.
questions.shortTrick: Use context: a fraud-awareness campaign educates.

questions.question: The regulator introduced stricter rules to ______ the misuse of customer data.
questions.solution: 'Curb' means control or restrain, which fits misuse of data.

questions.question: Despite the initial delay, the team completed the project with remarkable ______.
questions.solution: 'Efficiency' means accomplishing work effectively with minimal waste.
questions.shortTrick: Look for a positive work-performance noun.

questions.question: Water ______ in several districts has forced authorities to impose restrictions on consumption.
questions.solution: 'Scarcity' means shortage, which logically leads to consumption restrictions.

questions.question: The mobile application is ______ quick payments for small merchants.
questions.solution: 'Facilitating' means making something easier, so it fits quick payments.

questions.question: Many people ______ that success comes quickly, although it usually requires persistent effort.
questions.solution: 'Assume' means accept as true without proof and fits the contrast in the sentence.

questions.question: The unexpected policy change created considerable ______ among employees.
questions.solution: An unexpected change can create 'confusion'; the other nouns do not fit the context.

questions.question: The central bank decided to ______ interest rates unchanged for another month.
questions.solution: The natural construction is 'keep interest rates unchanged'.

questions.question: The officer responded ______ to the customer's complaint and resolved it the same day.
questions.solution: 'Promptly' means without delay and matches same-day resolution.

questions.question: The audit revealed several ______ in the way expenses had been recorded.
questions.solution: 'Irregularities' are departures from rules or normal procedure, appropriate in an audit context.

questions.question: She accepted the additional responsibility with great ______ and immediately began planning.
questions.solution: The immediate positive action supports 'enthusiasm'.

questions.question: The new software is expected to ______ the time required to process loan applications.
questions.solution: The intended benefit of software is to 'reduce' processing time.

questions.question: The manager tried to ______ the dispute before it affected the entire department.
questions.solution: 'Resolve a dispute' means settle it, fitting the aim of preventing wider impact.

questions.question: Customers were advised to remain ______ while clicking links received through unknown messages.
questions.solution: Unknown links pose risk, so 'cautious' is contextually correct.

questions.question: The committee sought an ______ assessment of the proposal before making its final decision.
questions.solution: An 'objective assessment' is impartial and evidence-based, appropriate before a decision.

questions.question: The authorities acted quickly to curb the spread of false information.
options: control the spread of false information
encourage the spread of false information
questions.solution: 'Curb' means restrain or control, so option 1 preserves the meaning.

questions.question: She tried to mask her disappointment after the final results were announced.
questions.solution: 'Mask' here means conceal or hide an emotion.

questions.question: The supervisor attempted to temper the employee's anger during the discussion.
questions.solution: 'Temper' as a verb here means moderate or reduce the intensity of anger.

questions.question: The company is looking forward to expand its operations in rural markets.
questions.solution: 'Look forward to' takes a noun or gerund, so 'to expanding' is correct.

questions.question: Hardly had the meeting begun than the power supply failed.
questions.solution: The standard correlative construction is 'Hardly...when'.

questions.question: The report is comprised of five sections covering different aspects of the project.
questions.solution: In formal exam grammar, use 'comprises five sections' or 'is composed of five sections'.
questions.shortTrick: Comprise does not need 'of' in active form.

questions.question: He has been working in this branch since three years.
questions.solution: Use 'for' with a duration and 'since' with a starting point.

questions.question: The new system is more easier to use than the previous one.
questions.solution: Do not use double comparatives. 'Much easier' correctly intensifies 'easier'.

questions.question: The manager insisted to review the documents before signing them.
questions.solution: 'Insist on' is followed by a noun or gerund: 'insisted on reviewing'.

questions.question: The agency offered (A) attractive discounts to explore (B) more travellers to encourage (C) new destinations.
questions.solution: The intended sentence is: 'The agency offered attractive discounts to encourage more travellers to explore new destinations.' Thus B and C swap: A-C-B.
questions.shortTrick: Read the whole sentence after each swap.

questions.question: The revised guidelines aim to enforcement (A) stronger ensure (B) and compliance (C) across branches.
questions.solution: Rearranging gives 'aim to ensure stronger enforcement and compliance across branches': B-A-C.
questions.shortTrick: Infinitive 'to' should be followed by a base verb.

questions.question: The training session helped employees awareness (A) practical develop (B) and skills (C) for handling fraud alerts.
questions.solution: The natural sentence is 'helped employees develop practical awareness and skills...': B-A-C.
questions.shortTrick: After 'helped employees', expect a base verb.

questions.question: The policy seeks to access (A) financial improve (B) for small businesses (C) in remote areas.
questions.solution: The intended phrase is 'seeks to improve financial access for small businesses': B-A-C.

questions.question: The officer assured the customer that the grievance would receive an immediate responce.
questions.solution: 'Responce' is misspelled; the correct spelling is 'response'.

questions.question: The probationer was asked to reconcile the daily transections before leaving the branch.
questions.solution: For financial dealings, the correct spelling is 'transactions'.

questions.question: The committee considered the proposal feasable after reviewing the revised cost estimates.
questions.solution: The correct spelling is 'feasible'.

questions.question: The manager appreciated her diligance in verifying every entry before submission.
questions.solution: The correct spelling is 'diligence'.

questions.question: The bank issued a seperate notice regarding the change in service charges.
questions.solution: The correct spelling is 'separate'.

questions.question: The branch arranged accomodation for employees attending the two-day workshop.
questions.solution: The correct spelling is 'accommodation' (double c, double m).

questions.question: Arrange the parts to form a meaningful sentence: (A) to improve customer service (B) the bank introduced (C) a new feedback system (D) across all its branches
questions.solution: B-C-D-A forms: 'The bank introduced a new feedback system across all its branches to improve customer service.'

questions.question: Arrange: (A) after several months of testing (B) the company finally launched (C) its digital payment platform (D) for small retailers
questions.solution: B-C-D-A gives a complete logical sentence.

questions.question: Arrange: (A) because online fraud is increasing (B) customers should verify (C) the authenticity of links (D) before entering personal details
questions.solution: B-C-D-A: Customers should verify the authenticity of links before entering personal details because online fraud is increasing.
questions.shortTrick: Modal subject clause gives a strong opening.

questions.question: Arrange: (A) during the quarterly review (B) several operational issues (C) were identified (D) by the audit team
questions.solution: B-C-D-A forms the natural passive sentence.

questions.question: Arrange: (A) without compromising security (B) banks are increasingly using automation (C) to process routine requests faster (D) and reduce manual workload
questions.solution: B-C-D-A: banks are using automation to process requests faster and reduce workload without compromising security.
questions.shortTrick: Purpose clauses usually follow the main clause.

questions.question: Arrange: (A) in remote areas (B) digital banking services (C) have expanded rapidly (D) over the past few years
questions.solution: B-C-D-A is grammatical and logical.

questions.question: Arrange: (A) before approving the loan (B) the officer carefully examined (C) the applicant's income records (D) and repayment history
questions.solution: B-C-D-A: the officer examined the records and history before approving the loan.
questions.shortTrick: Join objects before the time/purpose clause.

questions.question: Arrange: (A) even when market conditions change (B) a diversified portfolio (C) can help investors (D) manage risk more effectively
questions.solution: B-C-D-A creates the complete statement.

questions.question: Arrange: (A) to prevent unauthorized access (B) users are advised (C) to change their passwords regularly (D) and enable two-factor authentication
questions.solution: B-C-D-A is the natural order.
questions.shortTrick: 'Users are advised to...' starts the sentence.

questions.question: Arrange: (A) after receiving customer feedback (B) the developers modified (C) several features of the application (D) to make navigation simpler
questions.solution: B-C-D-A forms the most coherent sentence.
questions.shortTrick: Main action first; reason/time can come last.

questions.question: A community project can succeed when local residents actively ______ in planning and implementation.
questions.solution: 'Participate' means take part and fits both planning and implementation.

questions.question: The initiative initially progressed slowly because many residents remained ______ about its benefits.
questions.solution: 'Skeptical' means doubtful, fitting slow initial participation.

questions.question: When employment opportunities declined, families began to ______ alternative sources of income.
questions.solution: 'Seek' means look for, fitting alternative income sources.

questions.question: With more people contributing their labour, production increased ______ within a few months.
questions.solution: 'Significantly' appropriately describes a substantial increase.
questions.shortTrick: Increase significantly is a common collocation.

questions.question: The surplus produce was sold in nearby markets, ______ additional income for participating families.
questions.solution: Selling surplus produce generates income.

questions.question: The project demonstrated how collective effort can ______ a community's ability to face economic shocks.
questions.solution: Collective effort can strengthen ability/resilience.

questions.question: Researchers carefully scanned each object to ______ its structure without causing damage.
questions.solution: 'Examine' means inspect carefully and matches scanning.

questions.question: The collaboration offered valuable ______ into how earlier communities adapted to environmental change.
questions.solution: The fixed expression is 'valuable insights into'.

questions.question: The findings may ______ future research by identifying areas that require closer investigation.
questions.solution: Findings can 'guide' future research by directing attention.

questions.question: By combining different fields of study, the team developed a more ______ understanding of the evidence.
questions.solution: Combining fields supports a broader, more 'comprehensive' understanding.

questions.question: Passage: Many small retailers adopted digital payments because customers increasingly preferred cashless transactions. Although some owners initially worried about fees and technical problems, training programmes and simpler applications reduced these concerns. What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Small retailers are gradually adopting digital payments despite initial concerns.
Cash payments have been completely banned.
Technical problems make digital payments impossible.
Only large retailers benefit from digital payments.
questions.solution: The passage focuses on adoption by small retailers, initial concerns, and how those concerns were reduced.
questions.shortTrick: Main idea should cover the whole passage.

questions.question: Passage: A bank extended evening service hours at selected branches. Within three months, customer visits during the new hours increased steadily, especially among salaried workers. What can reasonably be inferred?
options: The extended hours are useful to customers who may be busy during normal working hours.
All customers stopped visiting during daytime.
The bank plans to close its branches.
Only retired customers use evening services.
questions.solution: The strong use by salaried workers suggests evening hours serve people occupied during normal hours.
questions.shortTrick: Inference must follow evidence, not imagination.

questions.question: Passage: The regulator asked lenders to adopt prudent practices while assessing risky loans. In the passage, 'prudent' most nearly means:
questions.solution: 'Prudent' means showing good judgment and caution.

questions.question: Passage: The training programme included modules on password security, phishing emails and safe use of public Wi-Fi. Which topic was NOT mentioned?
questions.solution: Investment planning does not appear in the listed modules.
questions.shortTrick: For NOT questions, verify every option.

questions.question: Passage: The municipality published weekly water-quality reports online so residents could see test results for their neighbourhoods. Why were the reports published online?
options: To make test information accessible to residents
To reduce the number of neighbourhoods
questions.solution: The stated purpose is to let residents see local test results.

questions.question: Passage: After a company allowed employees to choose two remote-working days each week, office attendance became lower on Fridays but project completion times did not increase. Which inference is best supported?
options: The flexible arrangement did not necessarily reduce project completion efficiency.
All employees prefer working only on Fridays.
The company no longer needs an office.
questions.solution: Completion times did not worsen despite changed attendance, so reduced office presence did not necessarily harm completion efficiency.
questions.shortTrick: Choose the cautious inference supported by evidence.

questions.question: Passage: The new recycling system has reduced waste sent to landfills, but officials acknowledge that participation remains uneven and further public awareness is needed. The tone is best described as:
questions.solution: The passage notes both improvement and remaining challenges, producing a balanced, cautiously positive tone.

questions.question: Passage: The bank introduced a simplified mobile interface for senior citizens. It uses larger text and fewer menu options. What does 'It' refer to?
questions.solution: The pronoun 'It' refers to the immediately preceding singular noun phrase, the simplified mobile interface.
questions.shortTrick: Trace pronouns to a logical antecedent.

questions.question: Passage: Urban trees reduce heat, absorb some air pollutants and provide shade for pedestrians. However, they require careful species selection and regular maintenance. Which statement best summarizes the passage?
options: Urban trees offer several benefits but require proper planning and care.
Urban trees have no environmental value.
Every tree species is suitable for every city.
questions.solution: The passage combines benefits with the need for careful selection and maintenance.
questions.shortTrick: A summary must include both sides.

questions.question: Passage: The sudden rise in demand placed considerable strain on the delivery network. Here, 'strain' most nearly means:
questions.solution: In this context, 'strain' means pressure or stress on capacity.
